memory_update.text: LOPE should remain the direct reference asset for the university enrollment/conversion stack because it discloses university partner services, technology/infrastructure support, online enrollment growth, and hybrid healthcare/workforce program growth.

NNI is an underfollowed second-order candidate: its ETSP segment touches tuition payment plans, school information systems, admissions/enrollment administrative software, and higher-education payment workflows, but education-conversion relevance requires segment-level verification.

ZETA is a speculative underfollowed supplier candidate for AI/data-driven education acquisition and lead conversion; current evidence is case-study based, so later layers must verify education vertical revenue and current customer concentration.

COUR is a small-cap distribution/credentialing platform candidate: it may benefit if universities increasingly need third-party learner discovery, credential metadata, and employer-aligned online degree pathways.

Call-center/BPO conversion quality remains a coverage gap. TTEC appeared relevant to enrollment-style customer acquisition and AI-enhanced CX, but its market cap was below $300M in the June 10, 2026 finance snapshot, so it should be treated only as a micro-cap speculative exception if revisited.

The node may split into four investable sub-nodes for later layers: direct university services and employer pipelines; education payments/admin workflow; AI/data-driven acquisition and identity; learner-distribution and credential platforms.

node: University enrollment, AI discovery, advising, and lead-conversion stack
summary: Expanded a focused universe for the university enrollment, AI discovery, advising, and lead-conversion stack. The cleanest direct reference asset is Grand Canyon Education, which explicitly provides post-secondary support services to university partners and reports strong online/hybrid enrollment growth. The underfollowed lane includes Nelnet for tuition/payment/admin infrastructure, Zeta Global for AI/data-driven education customer acquisition and enrollment marketing, and Coursera as a distribution/degree-program platform with university and industry partners. The main chokepoint hypothesis remains unproven: if AI search and lower-quality web leads weaken traditional student acquisition, value may migrate toward trusted employer channels, first-party data, compliant conversion workflows, payments/admin infrastructure, and platforms that already aggregate learners and university credentials.
